text: In the sow, the ovaries are small glands that produce ova (eggs); each ovary is surrounded by a thin membrane called the infundibulum, which collects ova and diverts them to the oviduct. The oviducts are 15–25 cm long and are the site of fertilization. The uterus consists of two horns up to 1.5 m long when carrying fetuses. The cervix is the muscular neck and entrance to the womb and can be open or closed. The vagina is the passageway from the exterior to the cervix; the bladder duct opens into the vagina. The vagina opens to the exterior through the fleshy lips of the vulva.
